questions.question: What is static pressure
options: The build-up of air pressure in a tube facing the airstream
The actual atmospheric pressure surrounding the aircraft
The difference between total pressure and ram pressure
questions.explain: Static pressure is simply the ambient atmospheric pressure around the aircraft.

questions.question: Most helicopters carry an extra item at their static ports. What is this item?
options: Special drain holes
Special cover plates
Special flapper plates
questions.explain: The manual names special cover plates.

questions.question: How are the static ports installed on the aircraft
options: Protruding from the skin on the sides of the aircraft
Flush with the skin on the nose of the aircraft
Flush with the skin on the sides of the aircraft
questions.explain: Static ports sit flush in the skin on the sides of the fuselage.

questions.question: Why do most helicopters have special cover plates at the static ports
options: To compensate the effects caused by the strong downwash of the rotor
To compensate the effects caused by the strong vibration of the rotor
To compensate the effects caused by the high angle of attack of the rotor
questions.explain: The cover plates offset the pressure effects of the rotor downwash.

questions.question: A technician is told that the static port zones must be absolutely clean and have a smooth surface. Which reason does the warning give?
options: So that no electrical heating current can be lost
So that no pressure distorting turbulences can occur
So that no water can enter the connected pressure lines
questions.explain: Dirt or roughness creates turbulence that distorts the sensed pressure.

questions.question: Why was the international standard atmosphere introduced
options: To have a uniform heating value for the probes
To have a uniform reference value for aviation
To have a correction table for high speed flight
questions.explain: The ISA gives aviation one common reference.

questions.question: Why are static ports placed in areas with low turbulence and ram air distortion
options: Because turbulence and ram air distortion block the static pressure hoses
Because turbulence and ram air distortion overheat the static port zones
Because turbulence and ram air distortion falsify the static pressure reading
questions.explain: Where such zones cannot be found the static pressure reading is affected, so a quiet zone keeps the reading true.

questions.question: What does the abbreviation SSE stand for
options: Standard source error
Static system error
Static source error
questions.explain: SSE is the static source error.

questions.question: Which pressure reading is affected by a static source error
options: The ram pressure reading
The total pressure reading
The static pressure reading
questions.explain: The SSE falsifies the static pressure reading.

questions.question: Why can a static source error arise on an aircraft
options: It is not always possible to find turbulence and ram air free zones on the aircraft
It is not always possible to keep the static ports electrically heated in flight
It is not always possible to calibrate the pneumatic devices to the ISA values
questions.explain: Where no turbulence free and ram air free zone exists, the sensed static pressure is falsified.

questions.question: An engineer is told that the static source error of a jet aeroplane is not a constant value. On which factors does it depend?
options: The mach number, the air density, the flap position and the outside air temperature
The mach number, the angle of attack, the flap position and the nose gear position
The mach number, the angle of attack, the rudder position and the nose gear position
questions.explain: These four items are the dependencies the manual lists for the SSE.

questions.question: A static source error falsifies the static pressure supplied to a simple pitot-static system. Which instruments are affected?
options: All three instruments of the simple system
Only the vertical speed indicator of the system
Only the airspeed indicator of the system
questions.explain: All three instruments of the simple system are supplied with static pressure, so all three are affected.

questions.question: What can happen to the static source error of a jet aeroplane flying near the speed of sound
options: It can exceed the tolerances required by law
It can fall below the tolerances required by law
It can become independent of the angle of attack
questions.explain: Close to the speed of sound the error may go beyond the legal tolerance.

questions.question: The static source error is listed with several dependencies. Which of them is marked as unusual?
options: The position of the flaps
The position of the nose gear
The angle of attack
questions.explain: Only the nose gear position carries the remark unusual.

questions.question: Which two pressures make up the total pressure Ptot
options: Ram pressure and differential pressure
Static pressure and differential pressure
Ram pressure and static pressure
questions.explain: The manual gives total pressure as ram pressure plus static pressure.

questions.question: What is pitot pressure
options: The actual atmospheric pressure in the air surrounding the aircraft
The build-up of air pressure in a tube with its opening facing the airstream
The build-up of air pressure in a tube with its opening across the airstream
questions.explain: Pitot pressure builds up in a tube whose opening points into the airstream.

questions.question: Ram pressure cannot be sensed on its own. Which pressure is already known from the static ports and is used to obtain it?
options: The total pressure Ptot
The dynamic pressure q
The static pressure ps
questions.explain: The static ports supply ps, which is subtracted from Ptot to leave q.

questions.question: How is ram pressure q obtained in the instrument
options: By measuring the static pressure at two separate static ports
By measuring the sum of the total pressure and the static pressure
By measuring the differential pressure between total and static pressure
questions.explain: Ram pressure is the difference between total and static pressure.

questions.question: What does electrical heating of the pitot tube prevent
options: The tube from freezing up
The tube from draining
The tube from deforming
questions.explain: The heater is there to stop the tube icing up.

questions.question: Where is the pitot tube usually located on the aircraft
options: Near the nose, on the wing leading edge or below the flaps
Near the tail, on the fin itself or below the rudder
Near the nose, on the nose itself or below the cockpit
questions.explain: These are the three locations the manual names.

questions.question: What do the small drain hole and the baffle of a pitot tube ensure
options: That ram air entering the tube is slowed down
That water entering the tube is drained away
That the tube inlet is kept free of any deformation
questions.explain: Their job is to get rid of water that has entered the tube.

questions.question: A student is worried that the drain hole in a pitot tube lets pressure escape. Which statement from the manual answers this?
options: The drain hole and the baffle do not affect the total pressure
The drain hole and the baffle slightly reduce the total pressure
The drain hole and the baffle slightly reduce the static pressure
questions.explain: The manual states in brackets that they do not affect the total pressure.

questions.question: Why is the Prandtl tube electrically heated
options: To prevent condensation
To prevent deformation
To prevent icing
questions.explain: Electrical heating keeps the probe free of ice.

questions.question: A Prandtl tube supplies both pressures from one probe. Where is it located on the aircraft?
options: At the rear of the aircraft
Under the wing of the aircraft
At the front of the aircraft
questions.explain: It sits at the front, like the pitot tube.

questions.question: What do the flapper plate and drain hole of a Prandtl tube prevent
options: Water from entering the pitot line
Icing from forming at the tube inlet
Roughness from forming on the tube surface
questions.explain: They keep water out of the pitot line.

questions.question: A Prandtl tube delivers total pressure and static pressure. Where is the required differential pressure obtained?
options: In the tube itself or in the piping
In the static port or in the drain hole
In the instrument or in a computer
questions.explain: The subtraction is done in the instrument or in a computer, not in the probe.

questions.question: How does a Prandtl tube obtain the ram pressure and static pressure needed for speed indication
options: From two separate measuring points
From one single ram air tube
From two connected static ports
questions.explain: The Prandtl tube takes both pressures at one single tube.

questions.question: An air data system receives three parameters from one single multi function probe. Which parameters are they?
options: Angle of attack, static air temperature and static pressure
Angle of sideslip, total air temperature and total pressure
Angle of attack, total air temperature and total pressure
questions.explain: AOA, TAT and total pressure are the three outputs of the probe.

questions.question: Which part of the multi function probe measures the angle of attack
options: A pitot probe
A TAT tube
A wind vane
questions.explain: The wind vane is the AOA sensing element.

questions.question: A multi function probe must deliver the total pressure to the air data system. Which of its parts provides this parameter?
options: The pitot probe
The temperature tube
The wind vane
questions.explain: The built-in pitot probe supplies the total pressure.

cards.question: Which pressure is used by an altimeter
options: Pitot and static pressure
Pitot pressure only
Static pressure only
cards.explain: The manual states the altimeter works on static pressure alone.

cards.question: An airspeed indicator in a simple system is connected to two pressure lines. Which pressures does it use?
options: Pitot pressure and static pressure
Pitot pressure and total pressure
Static pressure and differential pressure
cards.explain: The airspeed indicator is the only one of the three that needs both pitot and static pressure.

cards.question: A small aircraft is fitted with one pitot system and one static system. Which three instruments are supplied by it?
options: Altimeter, airspeed indicator and total air temperature gauge
Altimeter, vertical speed indicator and standby compass
Altimeter, vertical speed indicator and airspeed indicator
cards.explain: The simple system feeds exactly these three pitot-static instruments.

cards.question: How does pitot pressure reach the relevant instruments in a simple system
options: It is sensed by a pitot probe and guided via a tube to the instruments
It is sensed by a static port and guided via a tube to the instruments
It is sensed by a pitot probe and guided via a wind vane to the instruments
cards.explain: A pitot probe senses the pressure and a tube carries it to the instruments.

cards.question: Which instrument indicates the altitude of an aircraft
options: The altimeter
The airspeed indicator
The vertical speed indicator
cards.explain: The altimeter is the instrument the manual gives for altitude.

cards.question: Which pressure is used by a vertical speed indicator
options: Pitot and static pressure
Static pressure only
Pitot pressure only
cards.explain: The manual gives static pressure as the only supply of the vertical speed indicator.

cards.question: An airspeed indicator is fitted in a small aeroplane. What does this instrument indicate?
options: The altitude of the aircraft
The speed in the surrounding air
The vertical speed of the aircraft
cards.explain: The manual defines the airspeed indicator as showing the speed in the surrounding air.

cards.question: How many pitot systems and static systems does the simple system of a small aircraft have
options: One pitot system and two static systems
One pitot system and one static system
Two pitot systems and one static system
cards.explain: The simple system has exactly one of each.

cards.question: Where are the pressure measuring locations of one static pressure system situated
options: On the nose and the tail of the fuselage
On the upper and lower side of the fuselage
On the left and right hand side of the fuselage
cards.explain: Each static system has one measuring location on each side of the fuselage.

cards.question: How many separate pitot-static pressure systems are installed on modern commercial aircraft
options: One or two separate systems
Three or four separate systems
Two or three separate systems
cards.explain: The manual gives two or three separate systems.

cards.question: A maintenance manual lists the separate pitot-static pressure systems of a large aeroplane. How are they termed according to their allocation?
options: Captain's system, F/O's system and auxiliary system
Captain's system, purser's system and auxiliary system
Captain's system, F/O's system and alternate system
cards.explain: These are the three names given in the manual.

cards.question: In which small aircraft is the static source selector valve also found
options: Small single pilot aircraft certified for visual flight rules
Small two pilot aircraft certified for instrument flight rules
Small single pilot aircraft certified for instrument flight rules
cards.explain: The manual names single pilot aircraft certified for IFR.

cards.question: What does IFR stand for in the description of the static source selector valve
options: Instrument flight rules
Inertial flight rules
Instrument flight reference
cards.explain: The manual spells IFR out as instrument flight rules.

cards.question: What is static pressure
options: The build-up of air pressure in a tube facing the airstream
The actual atmospheric pressure surrounding the aircraft
The difference between total pressure and ram pressure
cards.explain: Static pressure is simply the ambient atmospheric pressure around the aircraft.

cards.question: Which authority introduced the international standard atmosphere
options: The international aviation authority ICAO
The international aviation authority EASA
The international aviation authority IATA
cards.explain: ICAO introduced the ISA.

cards.question: A pneumatic device is calibrated to the international standard atmosphere. Which value of air density at mean sea level applies?
cards.explain: The ISA sea level density given in the manual is 1,225 kg/m3.

cards.question: What are the ISA values of temperature and air pressure at mean sea level
options: 15 °C and 1225 mbar
20 °C and 1013 mbar
15 °C and 1013 mbar
cards.explain: The manual defines 15 °C and 1013 mbar at MSL.

cards.question: How are the static ports installed on the aircraft
options: Protruding from the skin on the sides of the aircraft
Flush with the skin on the nose of the aircraft
Flush with the skin on the sides of the aircraft
cards.explain: Static ports sit flush in the skin on the sides of the fuselage.

cards.question: What do some aircraft types have fitted at their static ports
options: Pneumatically heated static ports
Electrically drained static ports
Electrically heated static ports
cards.explain: The manual states that some types use electrically heated static ports.

cards.question: Where does the static pressure originate on the aircraft
options: In the static ports
In the pitot probe
In the drain hole
cards.explain: The static ports are the source of static pressure.

cards.question: At which level are the ISA values of density, temperature and pressure defined
options: At the cruise level
At mean sea level
At the tropopause
cards.explain: The manual gives the ISA figures for mean sea level.

cards.question: The current air pressure has to reach the individual air data measuring systems. How is it carried there?
options: Via hoses and pipes
Via a digital converter
Via a wind vane
cards.explain: Hoses and pipes carry the sensed pressure to the measuring systems.

cards.question: Most helicopters carry an extra item at their static ports. What is this item?
options: Special drain holes
Special cover plates
Special flapper plates
cards.explain: The manual names special cover plates.

cards.question: What does the abbreviation SSE stand for
options: Standard source error
Static system error
Static source error
cards.explain: SSE is the static source error.

cards.question: What is pitot pressure
options: The actual atmospheric pressure in the air surrounding the aircraft
The build-up of air pressure in a tube with its opening facing the airstream
The build-up of air pressure in a tube with its opening across the airstream
cards.explain: Pitot pressure builds up in a tube whose opening points into the airstream.

cards.question: Which two pressures make up the total pressure Ptot
options: Ram pressure and differential pressure
Static pressure and differential pressure
Ram pressure and static pressure
cards.explain: The manual gives total pressure as ram pressure plus static pressure.

cards.question: Which quantity does the symbol q represent in the pitot pressure relation
options: Ram pressure
Total pressure
Static pressure
cards.explain: The manual defines q as the ram pressure.

cards.question: Where is the pitot tube usually located on the aircraft
options: Near the nose, on the wing leading edge or below the flaps
Near the tail, on the fin itself or below the rudder
Near the nose, on the nose itself or below the cockpit
cards.explain: These are the three locations the manual names.

cards.question: What does the pitot tube consist of and which pressure is present in it during the entire flight
options: A cylindrical pipe in which total pressure Ptot is present
A cylindrical pipe in which static pressure Ps is present
A flapper plate chamber in which total pressure Ptot is present
cards.explain: It is a cylindrical pipe carrying total pressure throughout the flight.

cards.question: What does electrical heating of the pitot tube prevent
options: The tube from freezing up
The tube from draining
The tube from deforming
cards.explain: The heater is there to stop the tube icing up.

cards.question: How is the pressure in the pitot tube transferred to the interior of the aircraft
options: Via piping
Via a baffle
Via a drain hole
cards.explain: Piping carries the pressure from the tube into the aircraft.

cards.question: Why is the Prandtl tube electrically heated
options: To prevent condensation
To prevent deformation
To prevent icing
cards.explain: Electrical heating keeps the probe free of ice.

cards.question: A Prandtl tube supplies both pressures from one probe. Where is it located on the aircraft?
options: At the rear of the aircraft
Under the wing of the aircraft
At the front of the aircraft
cards.explain: It sits at the front, like the pitot tube.

cards.question: Through which part of the Prandtl tube does the total pressure enter
options: The holes in the sides
The flapper plate
The cylindrical inlet
cards.explain: Total pressure enters at the cylindrical inlet at the front.

cards.question: An air data system receives three parameters from one single multi function probe. Which parameters are they?
options: Angle of attack, static air temperature and static pressure
Angle of sideslip, total air temperature and total pressure
Angle of attack, total air temperature and total pressure
cards.explain: AOA, TAT and total pressure are the three outputs of the probe.

cards.question: Which part of the multi function probe measures the angle of attack
options: A pitot probe
A TAT tube
A wind vane
cards.explain: The wind vane is the AOA sensing element.

cards.question: Which part of the multi function probe measures the total air temperature
options: The wind vane of the probe
The tube of the probe
The pitot probe element
cards.explain: A tube inside the probe senses the total air temperature.

cards.question: Why are the left and right hand static pressure measuring locations of one static system connected to each other
options: To drain any water collected inside the static pressure lines
To compensate for any unbalance in pressure measurement
To increase the pressure delivered to the connected instruments
cards.explain: Cross-connecting the two sides evens out an unbalanced pressure reading between them.

cards.question: Why are modern commercial aircraft fitted with separate pitot-static pressure systems
options: For safety reasons
For calibration reasons
For weight reasons
cards.explain: Redundant systems are installed for safety.

cards.question: What does the alternate static source selector valve allow the Captain to do
options: Use the copilot's static pressure system
Use the copilot's pitot pressure system
Isolate the copilot's static pressure system
cards.explain: The valve switches the Captain over to the copilot's static source.

cards.question: The Captain's static system becomes faulty in flight. Which statement about switching over to the auxiliary system by means of the static air source selector valve is correct?
options: On every aircraft type the indicators can be switched to the auxiliary system
Only on a few aircraft types can the indicators be switched to the auxiliary system
Only on a few aircraft types can the indicators be switched to the pitot system
cards.explain: The manual restricts this switching possibility to a few aircraft types only.

cards.question: On which two quantities does air pressure p depend
options: Air density and temperature
Air density and mach number
Temperature and angle of attack
cards.explain: The manual lists air density and temperature as the two quantities.

cards.question: What is done with the ISA values defined at mean sea level
options: All pneumatic devices are corrected according to the flap position
All pneumatic devices are calibrated according to these values
All pneumatic devices are heated according to these values
cards.explain: The ISA values are the calibration reference for pneumatic devices.

cards.question: What do aircraft manufacturers ensure when they choose the position of the static ports
options: That they lie in areas with low temperature and air density variation
That they lie in areas with low turbulence and ram air distortion
That they lie in areas with high turbulence and ram air distortion
cards.explain: Low turbulence and low ram air distortion keep the static reading true.

cards.question: A technician is told that the static port zones must be absolutely clean and have a smooth surface. Which reason does the warning give?
options: So that no electrical heating current can be lost
So that no pressure distorting turbulences can occur
So that no water can enter the connected pressure lines
cards.explain: Dirt or roughness creates turbulence that distorts the sensed pressure.

cards.question: Why do most helicopters have special cover plates at the static ports
options: To compensate the effects caused by the strong downwash of the rotor
To compensate the effects caused by the strong vibration of the rotor
To compensate the effects caused by the high angle of attack of the rotor
cards.explain: The cover plates offset the pressure effects of the rotor downwash.

cards.question: Why was the international standard atmosphere introduced
options: To have a uniform heating value for the probes
To have a uniform reference value for aviation
To have a correction table for high speed flight
cards.explain: The ISA gives aviation one common reference.

cards.question: Why can a static source error arise on an aircraft
options: It is not always possible to find turbulence and ram air free zones on the aircraft
It is not always possible to keep the static ports electrically heated in flight
It is not always possible to calibrate the pneumatic devices to the ISA values
cards.explain: Where no turbulence free and ram air free zone exists, the sensed static pressure is falsified.

cards.question: An engineer is told that the static source error of a jet aeroplane is not a constant value. On which factors does it depend?
options: The mach number, the air density, the flap position and the outside air temperature
The mach number, the angle of attack, the flap position and the nose gear position
The mach number, the angle of attack, the rudder position and the nose gear position
cards.explain: These four items are the dependencies the manual lists for the SSE.

cards.question: How large is the static source error on slow-flying propeller planes
options: So small that it is negligible
So small that it must be measured
So large that it must be corrected
cards.explain: At low speed the error is negligible.

cards.question: The crew has to obtain the correct value from the distorted values being displayed. Where are the correction tables found?
options: In the Aircraft Maintenance Manual or in the flight log
In the Operating Manual or in the flight regulations
In the Operating Manual or in the weight and balance data
cards.explain: The manual names the Operating Manual and the flight regulations as the sources of the correction tables.

cards.question: What can make the static source error of one individual aircraft change over time
options: Recalibration changes to the air data computer
Surface changes to the static ports
Surface changes to the pitot probe inlet
cards.explain: Changes to the static port surfaces alter the error over the life of the aircraft.

cards.question: Which pressure reading is affected by a static source error
options: The ram pressure reading
The total pressure reading
The static pressure reading
cards.explain: The SSE falsifies the static pressure reading.

cards.question: The static source error is listed with several dependencies. Which of them is marked as unusual?
options: The position of the flaps
The position of the nose gear
The angle of attack
cards.explain: Only the nose gear position carries the remark unusual.

cards.question: What can happen to the static source error of a jet aeroplane flying near the speed of sound
options: It can exceed the tolerances required by law
It can fall below the tolerances required by law
It can become independent of the angle of attack
cards.explain: Close to the speed of sound the error may go beyond the legal tolerance.

cards.question: What do the correction tables enable the crew to do
options: Calibrate the pneumatic devices to the ISA values
Find the correct value from the distorted values displayed
Switch the indicators over to the auxiliary system
cards.explain: The tables turn a distorted indication back into the correct value.

cards.question: Two aeroplanes of the same type show different static source errors. Which statement matches the manual?
options: Deviations can occur only between different aircraft types
Deviations can occur within any one aircraft type
Deviations can occur only on slow-flying propeller planes
cards.explain: The manual allows for differences between individual aircraft of the same type.

cards.question: Which pressure alone is required to measure the speed of the aircraft in relation to the ambient air
options: The ram pressure q
The total pressure Ptot
The static pressure ps
cards.explain: Only the dynamic or ram pressure q is needed for speed measurement.

cards.question: How is ram pressure q obtained in the instrument
options: By measuring the static pressure at two separate static ports
By measuring the sum of the total pressure and the static pressure
By measuring the differential pressure between total and static pressure
cards.explain: Ram pressure is the difference between total and static pressure.

cards.question: Ram pressure cannot be sensed on its own. Which pressure is already known from the static ports and is used to obtain it?
options: The total pressure Ptot
The dynamic pressure q
The static pressure ps
cards.explain: The static ports supply ps, which is subtracted from Ptot to leave q.

cards.question: A pitot tube is being refitted to an aeroplane after removal. How must it be aligned?
options: So that it faces the predetermined airstream
So that it faces the predetermined rotor downwash
So that it lies across the predetermined airstream
cards.explain: The tube must point into the airstream to build up total pressure.

cards.question: What do the small drain hole and the baffle of a pitot tube ensure
options: That ram air entering the tube is slowed down
That water entering the tube is drained away
That the tube inlet is kept free of any deformation
cards.explain: Their job is to get rid of water that has entered the tube.

cards.question: A student is worried that the drain hole in a pitot tube lets pressure escape. Which statement from the manual answers this?
options: The drain hole and the baffle do not affect the total pressure
The drain hole and the baffle slightly reduce the total pressure
The drain hole and the baffle slightly reduce the static pressure
cards.explain: The manual states in brackets that they do not affect the total pressure.

cards.question: During a walk-around a technician finds a small dent at the inlet of a pitot tube. Which instruction from the manual applies?
options: The tube inlet may display slight deformation if the heating is serviceable
The tube inlet must not display any signs of deformation whatsoever
The tube inlet may display slight deformation if the drain hole is clear
cards.explain: The manual allows no deformation of the inlet at all.

cards.question: What does the Prandtl tube combine in one unit
options: A pitot tube with a sensor to measure total air temperature
A pitot tube with a sensor to measure static pressure
A static port with a sensor to measure the angle of attack
cards.explain: It puts the pitot function and a static pressure sensor into one probe.

cards.question: A Prandtl tube has a cylindrical inlet at the front and a row of holes drilled in its sides. What do these side holes supply?
options: Information for one or two connected pitot lines
Drainage for one or two connected water traps
Information for one or two connected static lines
cards.explain: The side holes feed the static lines, while the front inlet feeds total pressure.

cards.question: What do the flapper plate and drain hole of a Prandtl tube prevent
options: Water from entering the pitot line
Icing from forming at the tube inlet
Roughness from forming on the tube surface
cards.explain: They keep water out of the pitot line.

cards.question: A Prandtl tube is found with a rough surface after a repair. Which consequence does the manual warn about?
options: It will lead to heating element failures
It will lead to total pressure errors
It will lead to static pressure errors
cards.explain: Roughness disturbs the flow over the side holes and falsifies static pressure.

cards.question: A technician is about to touch a heated pitot or Prandtl tube shortly after the aircraft has landed. Which warning applies?
options: Risk of shock
Risk of icing
Risk of burns
cards.explain: The heated probe stays hot, so the manual warns of burns.

cards.question: How does a Prandtl tube obtain the ram pressure and static pressure needed for speed indication
options: From two separate measuring points
From one single ram air tube
From two connected static ports
cards.explain: The Prandtl tube takes both pressures at one single tube.

cards.question: Which two separate measuring points does the Prandtl tube replace
options: The pitot tube and the static port
The static port and the difference bellows
The pitot tube and the air data computer
cards.explain: The manual names the pitot tube and the static port as the two points it replaces.

cards.question: A Prandtl tube delivers total pressure and static pressure. Where is the required differential pressure obtained?
options: In the tube itself or in the piping
In the static port or in the drain hole
In the instrument or in a computer
cards.explain: The subtraction is done in the instrument or in a computer, not in the probe.

cards.question: A multi function probe must deliver the total pressure to the air data system. Which of its parts provides this parameter?
options: The pitot probe
The temperature tube
The wind vane
cards.explain: The built-in pitot probe supplies the total pressure.

cards.question: Each multi function probe has to pass its measured data to the related computer. Through which item does it do so?
options: Through the air data computer
Through the digital converter
Through the difference bellows
cards.explain: The digital converter is the link between the probe and the related computer.

cards.question: To which item does a multi function probe finally send its measured data
options: The related computer
The alternate static valve
The heated static port
cards.explain: The data ends up at the related computer.

cards.question: A technician traces one static pressure system of a small aeroplane and finds a measuring location on the left and on the right hand side of the fuselage. Which statement describes this arrangement correctly?
options: Each location belongs to a separate static system and they stay isolated
Both locations belong to the same pitot system and are connected together
Both locations belong to the same static system and are connected together
cards.explain: One static system uses both side locations and they are joined to each other.

cards.question: An aeroplane has a fault in one pilot's static system and is not one of the few types that can be switched to the auxiliary system. Which possibility remains?
options: Use of the pitot system via the selector valve
Use of the auxiliary system via the selector valve
Use of the other pilot's static system via the selector valve
cards.explain: Switching to the auxiliary system is limited to a few types, so the cross-over to the other pilot's static system is what remains.

cards.question: Why are static ports placed in areas with low turbulence and ram air distortion
options: Because turbulence and ram air distortion block the static pressure hoses
Because turbulence and ram air distortion overheat the static port zones
Because turbulence and ram air distortion falsify the static pressure reading
cards.explain: Where such zones cannot be found the static pressure reading is affected, so a quiet zone keeps the reading true.

cards.question: A jet aeroplane flies near to the speed of sound and its static source error exceeds the tolerances required by law. Which correction becomes necessary?
options: A correction using a differential pressure bellows
A correction using an air data computer
A correction using an alternate static source valve
cards.explain: The manual calls for an air data computer correction in this case.

cards.question: A static source error falsifies the static pressure supplied to a simple pitot-static system. Which instruments are affected?
options: All three instruments of the simple system
Only the vertical speed indicator of the system
Only the airspeed indicator of the system
cards.explain: All three instruments of the simple system are supplied with static pressure, so all three are affected.

cards.question: A slow-flying propeller aeroplane and a jet aeroplane near the speed of sound both have a static source error. Which comparison is correct?
options: Beyond the legal tolerance on both aeroplanes and corrected by the air data computer
Negligible on the propeller aeroplane and possibly beyond the legal tolerance on the jet
Negligible on the jet aeroplane and possibly beyond the legal tolerance on the propeller plane
cards.explain: The manual calls the error negligible at low speed and possibly beyond the legal tolerance near the speed of sound.
